added_failures_note: The reviewed run records no baseline_suite or after_suite block (both null; it is a measurement node), so no gate-log pair exists to subtract. The count is nevertheless derived rather than assumed: git diff --name-only 0f50140bbe..b038b345d -- nova/ tests/ returns 0 files, so the product and test trees at the reviewed head are identical to the base and the node cannot add a failing test id. The importing-test arm at main logs 46 failing ids across 11 of 45 files, all pre-existing at the base, which I re-derived from the run's own suite logs.

findings.text: the table's caption claims N = 7 recorded figures, all listed, none omitted, but the earlier receipt receipts/h200-repair.json carries seven keys including sample_vertex_count (340 entries, all 6), which the table omits, while vertex_partition is counted twice as groups and digest; the table therefore lists six of the seven keys and its completeness claim is false.

the launcher prints a literal EXIT=0 regardless of the per-file results, so a re-run of the recorded gate command logs a green exit even when files fail, and promotion reading that log's last line would record a false pass.

catch-all handling records any exception as a carrier refusal, which is how the driver's own AttributeError was published as a limited-carrier refusal in receipts/carrier-h200.json; the final ValueError measurement is correct but a driver bug is indistinguishable from a build limitation in the receipt.

the limited refusal is cited beside jobs 1297464/1297465, whose logs record an AttributeError at measure.py:248, while the ValueError at separatrix_clip.py:1950 actually came from jobs 1297476 and 1297480; the conclusion holds but the evidence trail points at logs that show a different refusal.

the driver duplicates the test module's _hex_sampling (measure_carrier.py:47) and vertex_partition (measure_carrier.py:64) rather than extending the owner, so the identity computation now lives twice and can drift from the test that pins it.
